title: Peek utility does not run
author: Emevic
summary: Peek and sometimes the PowerToys runner are inactive after sign-in until the tray UI is opened; the same report also describes Space invoking Peek during Explorer rename.

status.label: Needs startup-state evidence
status.detail: The report combines runner startup, Peek activation, and rename-focus symptoms that have different code paths.

next_action.label: Request Peek startup diagnostics
next_action.reason: Capture the untouched post-sign-in process and diagnostic state before opening the tray menu.

judgment.rationale: The original diagnostic is useful, but the report spans at least two failure boundaries and the only new comment adds no current version or state evidence.
evidence: The reporter says Peek begins working only after opening the PowerToys tray menu.
PowerToys sometimes does not appear to start automatically despite the setting being enabled.
Space can unexpectedly invoke Peek while renaming in Explorer.
The September follow-up only says the same behavior occurs.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a current post-sign-in process snapshot and a fresh /bugreport before the tray UI changes the state.

fix_assessment.rationale: A single fix cannot yet be selected because Runner startup, Peek registration, and Explorer rename suppression remain unresolved alternatives.

issue_context.summary: Peek is unavailable after some sign-ins until the tray UI is opened, and Space may also activate Peek during file rename.
known_information: The original report used a Store installation and included a June diagnostic archive.
Opening the tray UI changes the state and makes utilities work.
A second user confirmed the symptom without adding version or startup details.
inferences: The tray interaction may wake or reconnect a component, but the report does not establish whether the Runner, Peek process, or hotkey registration was missing.
issue_context.analysis: Evidence must be captured before opening the tray UI because that interaction removes the failing state. Rename activation should be confirmed separately rather than assumed to share the startup cause.
initial_investigation: Read the complete body and follow-up.
Checked labels, assignees, and linked closing pull requests; no current owner or closing PR is recorded.
Separated the startup and Explorer-focus symptoms into distinct diagnostic questions.

information_gaps.information: Whether PowerToys.exe and PowerToys.Peek.UI.exe are running immediately after an affected sign-in, before the tray menu is opened.
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes Runner startup failure from Peek process or hotkey registration failure.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Check Task Manager immediately after sign-in, before clicking the tray icon.

information_gaps.information: Fresh diagnostics from the untouched post-sign-in failure on the latest build.
information_gaps.why_needed: Shows startup, module launch, and hotkey-registration events before the tray interaction changes them.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Immediately after reproducing and before opening the tray menu, submit a comment containing /bugreport.

actions.label: Request Peek startup diagnostics

comment.body:
Thanks for the original diagnostic and for confirming that opening the tray menu changes the behavior.

**Needed**
1. On the latest stable or Preview build, please reproduce an affected sign-in and, before clicking the PowerToys tray icon, confirm whether `PowerToys.exe` and `PowerToys.Peek.UI.exe` are running in Task Manager.
2. In that same untouched state, please submit a comment containing `/bugreport` so the generated ZIP captures startup and hotkey-registration events.

This will distinguish Runner startup failure from Peek process or hotkey-registration failure.

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.
